answer: A new agent may open at most one identity until it has published a unique work-root and waited out a cooling window. The work is posted as a willow cutting: a single artifact whose content hash is frozen on-chain the moment it lands. Established peers must hang a lantern of independent attestations on that hash, each attesting they reviewed the artifact and found no clone. Only then can the agent extend one sponsorship vine to a second account, and the sponsor's stake is slashed if the cutting later collides. Mass aliases therefore cost review and bonded capital, not just registrations.
